subject: error compiling model when variable declared as type "cholesky_factor_cov"

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: error compiling model when variable declared as type "cholesky_factor_cov"
parts:
Hello Stanimals,

Is the constrained variable type "cholesky_factor_cov" actually implemented yet?  When I try to declare a variable of that type, the model does not compile (I'm using rstan::stan_model() ).   I've tried declaring it as cholesky_factor_cov[P] and cholesky_factor_cov[P,P], as described on p. 211 of the manual, with the same result.  When I simply declare the same variable as type matrix[P,P] (as seen in numerous examples in the manual, e.g., pages 145-146, 149-151, 183-186), then the model compiles (and samples) fine, even though I change nothing else, assigning the same value(s) to it in the syntax.

Below (and attached) is a model that gives and error message when I try to compile it, which I pasted below the model syntax.

data {
  int N; // N subjects
  int P; // P variables
  vector[P] X[N]; // data
}
parameters {
  vector[P] myMeans;
  vector[P] mySDs;
  corr_matrix[P] Rho;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[P] mu[N]; // expected values for each subject
  cholesky_factor_cov[P] sigmaChol;
 
  sigmaChol <- diag_matrix(mySDs) * cholesky_decompose(Rho);
}
model {
  for (n in 1:N)
    X[n] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu[n], sigmaChol);
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: error compiling model when variable declared as type "cholesky_factor_cov"
parts:
We just can't spell cholesky correctly. It has been fixed for a long time in the develop branch and should be released soon. For now, you can just declare it to be a regular matrix.

Ben
